speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see your infant is having bilious vomiting and cannot pass meconium, which is concerning. Can you tell me exactly how old your baby is and when the vomiting started?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease (congenital aganglionic megacolon).

The combination of failure to pass meconium within 48 hours, bilious vomiting, and abdominal distension in a newborn is highly suggestive of Hirschsprung disease. I am requesting an abdominal X-ray to confirm the presence of a distal obstruction and dilated loops of bowel. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.
